newsitem.title: USA: Forcenergy sees doubling of revenues.
newsitem.headline: Forcenergy sees doubling of revenues.

text.p: Forcenergy Inc expects revenues and cash flow to double this year on an 81 percent increase in production, chief executive Stig Wennerstrom told PaineWebber's annual energy conference.
That increase would put 1997 production at 96 billion cubic feet equivalent from reserves estimated to total 607 billion cubic feet equivalent, he said.
Including the Great Western Resources acquisition completed last month, Wennerstrom said, revenues are expected to increase 100 percent to $257 million and cash flow 101 percent to $139 million.
Production averaged 273 million cubic feet per day equivalent last month, he said, adding this included 144 million cubic feet of natural gas and 21,460 barrels of liquids per day.
He said 74 percent of that came from the Gulf of Mexico and another 16 percent from Alaska's Cook Inlet, while the remaining 10 percent was from the U.S. onshore.
Wennerstrom also said the company wants to maintain debt at less than 50 percent of capitalization over time.
Noting debt was at 35 percent before the company's latest acquisitions, he said it is now between 59 and 60 percent.

J. Russell Porter, vice president - corporate development, said Forcenergy would "delever (the debt ratio) when the stock is more attractive," but did not say what stock price was needed before sales would be considered.
He said the company has additional credit flexibility, including a $200 million credit facility with nothing drawn down.

Although neither official discussed the company's earnings outlook, Porter did say each 10 million cubic feet per day change in natural gas production or 1,000 barrel per day change in oil production would change annual earnings by $0.12 per share.

And each $0.10 per thousand cubic feet change in natural gas prices has an impact of $0.18 per share, while each $1 per barrel oil price change is reflected with a $0.22 per share change in annual earnings, he said.
Forcenergy Inc is an affiliate of Forcenergy AB.
